test_title: PYST 56: SSC GD Constable - English (Held on: 13th December 2021 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I prevailed / upto him / to join / our team.
solution:
The correct option is "Upto him".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, "upto him" segment contains a grammatical error
 
• The original sentence was "I prevailed upto him to join our team." The error in this sentence is the use of "upto" instead of "upon." "Upto" is not a recognized preposition in Standard English. Instead, "upon" should be used, as it is the correct preposition to use with the verb "prevail."
 
• In this sentence, the word "prevailed" means that the speaker succeeded in convincing the other person to join their team. Therefore, the corrected sentence means that the speaker was able to persuade the other person to join their team.
 
• So the corrected sentence is "I prevailed upon him to join our team." Here, "upon" means "on," "over," or "above," and it is used to indicate that one person has succeeded in convincing or persuading another person to do something.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
 

 
When a set of words are written down, a*** sentence*** is one that starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark.

 

 
• The majority of sentences have a ***subject*** and a ***verb***.
 
• The main types of sentences are:
 
 
• ***Simple sentence***
 
• ***Complex sentence***
 
• ***Compound sentence***
